Subject: Closeflow: Load qualification & MAP — evaluation delivery and next steps

Lucy — thanks again for the time today. Per our MAP, attaching the evaluation plan we discussed (redwood_map_eval_plan_v3.xlsx). High-level notes: 

- Goal: validate latency/throughput and TTFT targets for ACME's inference workload under both burst and steady-state patterns; produce a short runbook for rate-limit tuning.
- Test window: 12/14–12/15 (two short windows: burst probes on day 1; sustained runs on day 2).
- Primary SLOs: p95 latency < 250ms for 512-token responses; steady-state throughput >= 120 requests/sec per dedicated slice; TTFT < 50ms cold start target for warmed slices.

Concrete asks from ACME: 1) confirm the list of test prompts and max sequence length (I used the examples you shared), 2) grant temporary API keys scoped to a dedicated test slice, and 3) give ops a time window for a 20-minute capacity spike.

I've included Priyom on the thread to coordinate the exact slot for the spike and Lauren to capture results and slide the summary into our MAP. If those test windows work for you we'll proceed to schedule the probe slots in the portal and send the scoped keys.

Best,
Michael
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

1) Prompts: the set attached to this reply (acme_test_prompts.txt) includes 3 heavy multi-turn threads we want to prioritize. All responses should be capped at 600 tokens.
2) Spike window: can we do the burst probe on 12/14 10:00–10:30 PST? Ops wants a 10-minute heads-up before the spike.
3) Steady-state: we prefer 12/15 14:00–15:30 PST for a 90-minute ramp to steady 110–130 req/s.

Also: we need a short statement about how rate-limiting will behave during the burst vs. steady run so our backend can detect and surface fallbacks properly.

Lucy — confirmed on the windows. Quick operational notes ahead of the probe:

- Burst probe (12/14 10:00 PST): we'll provision a dedicated slice with reserved capacity + a short autoscale headroom for the 30-min window. We'll send scoped API keys 24 hours before the probe; ops will post the 10-minute countdown in the channel.
- Behavior during burst vs steady: Redwood enforces per-API-key token bucket throttling at the slice level. For the probe we will: 1) loosen burst_token_limit to allow short peaks to absorb the probe, 2) keep steady_rate_limit at the configured commit for sustained runs. If the probe exceeds the burst buffer, requests will return HTTP 429 with Retry-After and an explanatory header (X-Redwood-Limit-Info).
- Canary fallback: if p95 latency breaches 450ms for more than 2 consecutive minutes we will automatically divert traffic to a smaller-latency model variant (same output shape) and mark the run as degraded in the MAP report.

Lauren will capture the exact token bucket settings and include them in the runbook.

Thanks — Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Ramos <lucy.ramos@acmeai.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-16T11:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Closeflow: Load qualification & MAP — evaluation delivery and next steps

Hi all — running summary and raw CSV attached. Short version: burst probe behaved as expected; steady-state run revealed queueing at 125–130 req/s for the 600-token cap prompt set.

Key findings (see attached acme_concurrency_probe_results.csv for timestamps and per-request metrics):
- Burst probe (12/14 10:00–10:30): peaked at 420 req/min (7 req/s) per client process; platform absorbed the spike with transient p95 latency up to 380ms, then stabilized under 260ms after autoscale warmed slices. No 429s observed during the 30-minute window.
- Steady-state (12/15 14:00–15:30): target 110–130 req/s across test clients. At sustained 125–130 req/s we observed queue growth (median queue length 140ms at 125 req/s, rising to 520ms at 130 req/s) and p95 latency drifting above 300ms. A configuration tweak that reduced per-slice max inflight from 32->24 and increased number of concurrent slices by 1 reduced p95 by ~18% and flattened queue growth.
- TTFT: cold start TTFT remained within 60–80ms for newly created warmed slices; our earlier target of <50ms is achievable with a slightly different warm policy (pre-warm timeout decreased).

Action items we recommend for ACME before signing: 
1) Adopt a hybrid rate cap: 120 req/s per logical group with burst buffer of +15% for short probes.
2) Set per-slice inflight max to 24 for 600-token responses; allow dynamic slice increments during scheduled steady runs.
3) Add a short-lived pre-warm policy tied to your first minute of steady traffic to meet the <50ms TTFT target.

We'll fold these into the MAP slides and send an executive one-pager. Attaching: acme_concurrency_probe_results.csv and closeflow_summary_slide.pdf.

Thanks,
Lauren
Performance PM, Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_concurrency_probe_results.csv, closeflow_summary_slide.pdf
